_meta.method: 5-agent contract-review team; each agent contract verified against the canonical sources in rank order: .claude/contracts/ tier docs, src/agents/<name>/CONTRACT_VALIDATION.md, and the implementation (agent.py / graph.py / nodes) with file:line evidence. Where doc and implementation disagree, the implementation is today's truth and the discrepancy is listed under 'mismatches'.
_meta.consumers: scripts/benchmarks/routing/gen_judge_review.py (human-review worksheet) and the #1337 Step 0 gold-judge prompt. Single source of truth for contract text in the routing benchmark.
boundary_notes: health_score vs drift_monitor: the prior 'health_score = NOT ML-model quality' premise is WRONG. health_score HAS a model-health dimension (model_health.py + ModelMetrics accuracy/precision/recall/f1/auc) - it scores whether deployed models are performing acceptably RIGHT NOW against fixed thresholds (point-in-time operational snapshot). drift_monitor owns TEMPORAL/DISTRIBUTIONAL SHIFT vs a baseline (PSI/KS/chi-square on prediction distributions, concept drift, causal-DAG structural drift). Router keyword split proves it: 'model.*perform'->system_health(health_score), 'model.*degrad'->drift_check(drift_monitor). Practical reviewer rule: 'is model X healthy / what's its accuracy' = health_score; 'has model X drifted/degraded/PSI/distribution-shift over time' = drift_monitor.

All FOUR agents ARE wired into INTENT_TO_AGENTS and reachable from intent_classifier keyword patterns - the 'believed UNMAPPED' premise is FALSE for every one of them. drift_check->drift_monitor (critical/10s), system_health->health_score (critical/5s), resource_allocation->resource_optimizer (critical/20s, plus 'high' in the performance_gap+resource_allocation multi-agent pattern), feedback->feedback_learner (critical/30s). CONTRACT_VALIDATION.md exists for all four.

'Unmapped agents' in #1337 means unmapped in the 4-stage classifier's DOMAIN_TO_AGENT (8 domains only, pattern_selector.py:26-38): resource_optimizer, health_score, feedback_learner, experiment_monitor have no classifier Domain. ALL 14 chat agents ARE reachable via the legacy router INTENT_TO_AGENTS - the gap is classifier coverage, not prod reachability.

cohort_constructor.purpose: Tier-0 ML-pipeline agent that applies FDA/EMA-label inclusion/exclusion criteria to a real patient DataFrame to materialize an eligible cohort (patient IDs + eligibility audit trail + temporal lookback/followup validation) for downstream ML training.
covers: Given structured study params + a patient DataFrame, produce the list of eligible patient_journey_ids for a brand/indication (Remibrutinib/CSU, Fabhalta/PNH, Kisqali/HR+HER2-)
Apply AND inclusion / AND-NOT exclusion criteria with a per-criterion eligibility log (removed/remaining counts)
Validate temporal eligibility (lookback_days/followup_days) and emit exclusion stats + config_hash for reproducibility
Hand off cohort_spec + eligible_patient_ids to data_preparer
does_not_cover: Chat/free-text 'how many patients are eligible / size the cohort' questions -> owned by cohort_profiler (constructor cannot run from a chat payload; its resolver fails closed)
Natural-language explanation of an analysis -> owned by explainer
Upstream study-scoping (target var, problem type, brand/indication) -> owned by scope_definer (its upstream)
Downstream feature/QC prep on the eligible set -> owned by data_preparer (its downstream)
cohort_constructor.internal_pipeline: LangGraph single dispatch, NO LLM: validate_config -> apply_criteria -> validate_temporal -> generate_metadata -> END (conditional error_handler branch); real entry point is run(patient_df, brand, indication, config)/run_sync, SLA <120s per 100K patients.
cohort_constructor.dispatch: NOT in INTENT_TO_AGENTS -> pipeline-only, not chat-routable. It IS listed in VALID_AGENTS so a chat route could name it, but its dispatcher resolver _resolve_cohort_constructor_input ALWAYS returns NeedsStructuredInput (fails closed with an actionable 'use the ML cohort pipeline' message, missing=('patient_df','brand')). Deliberately NOT in AGENT_METHOD_MAP (Tier 1-5 only); would otherwise fall to default 'analyze', which it doesn't implement. Net: can NEVER be a valid gold routing target for a chat query.
mismatches: Contract doc (tier0/cohort_constructor.md) frames a rich request/response contract as if chat/orchestrator-callable; implementation reality is that any chat dispatch fails closed by design (resolver returns NeedsStructuredInput). Doc = pipeline intent, impl = pipeline-only + chat-guard.
Doc positions scope_definer -> cohort_constructor -> data_preparer and Tier-0 ML Foundation, consistent with impl; no functional discrepancy beyond the routability nuance.

cohort_profiler.purpose: Tier-0 chat companion to cohort_constructor that answers the free-text 'size / define a cohort' question with REAL DB-backed counts, never fabricating. Patient path: new-Rx headline + severity tier + line-of-therapy breakdown for one brand or all brands. Since the ratified extend ruling (2026-07-29, implemented in #1356 parts 1+2): the ask's parameters BIND into the profile query — brand (named directly or via indication, e.g. 'CSU' -> Remibrutinib) and servable inclusion criteria (age-at-diagnosis bounds), with an HONEST accounting naming exactly which criteria were applied and which could not be (e.g. 'diagnosed in 2024' — no true diagnosis dates exist — fails closed with guidance, never answers a different question). HCP path: HCP-entity cohorts with quantitative KPI thresholds ('HCPs who prescribed >50 TRx last quarter') via per-HCP TRx aggregation over an explicit half-open time window with a threshold filter, returning cohort size + specialty / priority-tier breakdowns mirroring the patient-profile shape.
covers: How many patients are eligible / in the Remibrutinib (or Fabhalta / Kisqali) prescribing population?
Size / define the cohort for <brand> (brand binds from the query text or indication mention when no structured entity was grounded)
Break down the <brand> population by disease-severity tier (low/medium/high)
Break down the <brand> population by line of therapy (0/1/2/3+ prior lines)
Same across all supported brands when no brand is named in the query
Patient cohorts with servable inclusion criteria bound into the query: brand + age-at-diagnosis bounds ('adults over 18'), with per-criterion applied / not-applied accounting (#1356 part 1)

HCP-entity cohorts with quantitative KPI thresholds over an explicit time window: 'HCPs who prescribed more than 50 TRx last quarter' -> per-HCP TRx aggregation (same treatment_events prescription substrate as the platform TRx KPI), threshold filter, cohort size + specialty / priority-tier breakdowns; honest zero when the threshold filters everyone out of a nonzero prescribing base (#1356 part 2)
does_not_cover: Materializing the actual eligible patient rows / IDs with FDA-EMA criteria + audit trail for an ML pipeline -> owned by cohort_constructor
Explaining an upstream analysis in narrative form -> owned by explainer
Arbitrary KPI/metric questions beyond cohort sizing -> the domain KPI agents (e.g. gap_analyzer) / chat KPI tool

Criteria the data model cannot serve (e.g. diagnosis-year filters: zero 'diagnosis' events, no diagnosis-date column) -> named honestly as NOT applied with guidance; if nothing in the ask can be served it fails closed rather than return a canned profile
Adoption-propensity ('model-scored high-value') HCP ranking -> #1356 part 3, blocked on #1354 promotion of the hcp_adoption_* models; today 'high-value' is threshold-filtered TRx volume only
cohort_profiler.internal_pipeline: Single dispatch, pure async computation, NO graph/LLM: analyze() -> parse_cohort_ask (ask.py: entity patient|hcp, brand via hint -> query text -> indication, age criteria, diagnosis-year [recognized, unservable], TRx threshold, window with explicit dates) -> three paths: (a) criteria-less patient ask keeps the mig-105 KPI-calculator path [headline NRx WS3-BI-006 + 3 severity + 4 line calls via asyncio.to_thread, <=8 per brand — numbers stay in lock-step with the live chat UI, and the bound brand keys the Redis KPI cache context]; (b) criteria-bound patient ask runs the allowlisted cohort_profiler_patient_criteria_profile statement (migration 117, kpi_query RPC — params brand/min-age/max-age) grouped by (segment_assignment, prior_therapy_lines); (c) HCP ask runs cohort_profiler_hcp_trx_cohort (params brand/window-start/window-end/exclusive-TRx-floor) grouped by (specialty, priority_tier), with a threshold-free probe distinguishing an honest zero-match from a genuine empty. Fails closed only on genuine empty / unservable-only asks; every path binds the ask parameters so two different asks can never share a cached payload (the q11/q15 byte-identical 26ms defect).
cohort_profiler.dispatch: INTENT_TO_AGENTS['cohort_definition'] -> cohort_profiler, criticality 'critical', timeout_ms=30000, fallback_agent=None (router.py:176-184). 4-stage active classifier: pattern_selector Domain.COHORT_DEFINITION -> cohort_profiler. Resolver _resolve_cohort_profiler_input grounds an optional brand and NEVER fails closed at resolve time; it IS in _FAIL_CLOSED_ON_FAILED_STATUS so an honest empty (status='failed') fails the dispatch rather than laundering a blank profile. Dispatches via default 'analyze' method (intentionally NOT in AGENT_METHOD_MAP -> Tier-0 fall-through); narrative field via AGENT_RESPONSE_FIELDS.
cohort_profiler.distilled_line_verdict: correct: accurate but add specificity -- it reports population SIZES not a patient list, reuses the mig-105 KPI-calculator path (WS3-BI-006 NRx) so numbers match live chat, and it fails closed (not zero-narrates) when a brand has no prescribing population. Patient segment axes are severity tier AND line-of-therapy; since #1356 the HCP path adds specialty AND priority-tier axes, and asks bind brand / criteria / threshold / window parameters.

tool_composer.purpose: Tier-1 orchestration agent that answers a MULTI-FACETED query via a 4-phase pipeline (DECOMPOSE -> PLAN -> EXECUTE -> SYNTHESIZE): break the query into 2-6 atomic sub-questions with a dependency DAG, map each sub-question to a registered tool/agent-capability, execute tools in dependency order with retry + circuit-breaker resilience, and synthesize ONE coherent answer with confidence/citations/caveats. It composes OTHER agents' capabilities; it does not compute the analytics itself.
covers: Decomposing a multi-faceted query into 2-6 atomic sub-questions with a DAG (tier1-tool-composer-contracts.md:16-19, 96-116; decomposer.py)

Planning: mapping each sub-question to a tool across MULTIPLE agent capabilities via the ToolRegistry (planner.py; CONTRACT_VALIDATION.md:8; categories CAUSAL/SEGMENTATION/GAP/EXPERIMENT/PREDICTION/MONITORING/EXPLANATION)
Dependency-ordered execution with resilience: exponential backoff, circuit breaker, parallel groups (executor.py; tier1-tool-composer-contracts.md:336-529)
Synthesis of cross-domain results into one NL answer with confidence, citations, caveats (synthesizer.py; ComposedResponse)
Invoked ONLY when routing classifies the query as MULTI_FACETED / multi-domain-with-dependencies (agent.py:245-247)
does_not_cover: Single-domain queries EVEN multi-STEP ones. A single mapped domain/intent always routes SINGLE_AGENT to the domain agent (e.g. causal_impact), which runs its OWN multi-step internal pipeline under one dispatch (pattern_selector.py:127-147)
Independent multi-domain queries with NO dependencies -> route PARALLEL_DELEGATION, not tool_composer (pattern_selector.py:165-192)
The routing decision itself: RouterNode/classifier decides; tool_composer is a target, and 'multi_faceted' is a META-signal, NOT an agent domain (router.py:284-298)
The underlying analytical methods (DoWhy/EconML, SHAP, forecasting): it calls other agents' registered tools
Ambiguity resolution: that is CLARIFICATION_NEEDED, decided upstream in Stage 4
tool_composer.internal_pipeline: 4 phases, each with its own handler and (for 3 of them) an LLM call: QueryDecomposer (decomposer.py, ~0.3 temp), ToolPlanner (planner.py, ~0.2 temp), PlanExecutor (executor.py, NO LLM - runs tools with backoff + circuit breaker + parallel groups), ResponseSynthesizer (synthesizer.py, ~0.4 temp). SLA 180s (10/15/120/30s per phase). CRITICAL NUANCE for the judge: heavy single-domain agents (causal_impact, heterogeneous_optimizer, cohort_profiler) ALSO run multi-step pipelines internally under ONE dispatch - that internal multi-step-ness is NOT tool_composer's trigger.
tool_composer.dispatch: Reached two ways, both converging on the same dispatch. (1) Legacy: IntentClassifierNode sets primary_intent='multi_faceted' -> router.py INTENT_TO_AGENTS['multi_faceted'] = tool_composer, priority=critical, timeout_ms=180000, fallback_agent='explainer' (router.py:159-168, 296-298). (2) 4-stage active mode: pattern=='TOOL_COMPOSER' -> router.py _dispatch_from_classification reuses that same canonical dispatch (router.py:451-458). Entry point ToolComposerAgent.run({query, context}) -> composer.compose(). NOTE: classifier-detected sub_questions/dependencies are NOT currently threaded into tool_composer params (router.py:451-458 comment) - tool_composer re-decomposes from scratch.
tool_composer.distilled_line_verdict: correct: 'Decomposes multi-faceted queries, plans + executes across multiple agent capabilities, synthesizes one answer. Warranted only when no single agent's contract covers the ask' is RIGHT on the necessary condition (no single agent covers the ask). Tighten to the platform's operative test: the ask must span >=2 DISTINCT agent-capability domains (or >=2 distinct strong intents) AND those cross-domain sub-questions must be dependency-linked. If >=2 domains but NO dependency between them, it is PARALLEL_DELEGATION, not TOOL_COMPOSER. Cross-domain spanning makes it not-single-agent; the dependency makes it tool_composer rather than parallel.
mismatches: The tier1 contract doc frames tool_composer around its Phase-1 decomposition mechanic (2-6 sub-questions + DAG) without restating the multi-DOMAIN routing GATE. Read alone, the doc invites 'any dependent multi-step query' - exactly the misread the LLM judge made. The gate lives ONLY in the classifier code, not the contract doc.
The distilled line does not surface that PARALLEL_DELEGATION ALSO spans multiple agent capabilities; only the dependency link separates the two.

causal_impact.purpose: Estimates the average causal effect of a single treatment on an outcome using DoWhy/EconML, then validates it with refutation and sensitivity tests and renders a natural-language interpretation.
covers: What is the causal effect of HCP engagement frequency on TRx (ATE + 95% CI + p-value)?
Does increasing copay assistance actually cause higher adherence once we control for these confounders?
Is this relationship causal or just correlation - does the effect survive placebo / random-common-cause / subset refutation?
How sensitive is the estimated effect to unmeasured confounding (E-value / robustness value)?
Build (or auto-discover) the causal DAG for treatment X on outcome Y and estimate the adjusted effect.
does_not_cover: Which segments respond best / how the effect varies across segments (deep CATE + responder discovery) - owned by heterogeneous_optimizer (causal_impact only emits an optional cate_by_segment hint and hands off).
Where the biggest ROI/performance-gap opportunities are and their payback - owned by gap_analyzer.
Designing an A/B test or pre-registration to validate the effect - owned by experiment_designer.
Forecasting/predicting future outcome values - owned by prediction_synthesizer.
Solving optimal budget/resource allocation across territories - owned by resource_optimizer.
causal_impact.internal_pipeline: audit_init -> graph_builder (DAG build, optional V4.4 structure auto-discovery) -> adjustment_set_policy -> estimation (DoWhy/EconML ATE) -> refutation (conditional; may skip to interpretation on failure) -> sensitivity (E-value) -> interpretation (NL narrative) -> END - all one SINGLE_AGENT dispatch.
causal_impact.dispatch: INTENT_TO_AGENTS['causal_effect'] -> causal_impact, criticality 'critical' (timeout 30s, fallback_agent='explainer'); also first leg of MULTI_AGENT_PATTERNS[('causal_effect','segment_analysis')] as 'critical' (paired with heterogeneous_optimizer 'high').
causal_impact.distilled_line_verdict: correct: pipeline is 6 business stages, not 5 - the distilled line omits the adjustment_set_policy stage (between DAG build and estimation) and that DAG build can run auto-discovery (structure learning). Refutation is conditional (skippable on estimation failure). CATE is only an optional side-output hint here, not the agent's job - the '/CATE estimation' phrasing overstates it (heterogeneous_optimizer owns CATE).
mismatches: Contract latency says 'Up to 120s' but router SLA for causal_effect is 30000ms; the doc's own header (60s compute + 30s interp) also disagrees with the 30s dispatch timeout.

Contract lists a fixed estimation_method default 'backdoor.econml.dml.CausalForestDML' and no auto-discovery in 2.x prose, but implementation supports auto_discover/DAG structure learning (V4.4) as a real graph_builder path.
Implementation adds an audit_init genesis node and an adjustment_set_policy node not enumerated as pipeline stages in the tier-2 contract.

gap_analyzer.purpose: Detects performance gaps across segments for a brand, estimates ROI/payback to close each gap, and prioritizes the opportunities into actionable buckets (quick wins, steady plays, strategic bets) with value-destroying ones suppressed.
covers: Where are the biggest ROI opportunities for Kisqali?
Which regions/specialties/deciles have the largest performance gaps vs potential (or vs target/benchmark)?
What's the ROI, payback period, and difficulty of closing each gap, and which are quick wins vs strategic bets?
Rank our opportunities by expected revenue impact and tell me the total addressable value.
does_not_cover: Whether closing a gap will *causally* lift the outcome / estimating the intervention's treatment effect - owned by causal_impact (gap_analyzer suggests it as validation).
Which segments respond best to an intervention (treatment-effect heterogeneity / CATE) - owned by heterogeneous_optimizer.
Designing a controlled experiment to validate the top opportunity - owned by experiment_designer (its default suggested_next_agent).
Running the constrained optimal-allocation solver to distribute a fixed budget across opportunities - owned by resource_optimizer (gap_analyzer sizes/prioritizes but does not solve the allocation).
gap_analyzer.internal_pipeline: audit_init -> gap_detector -> roi_calculator -> instrument_analyzer (#357, real IV first-stage F-test strength) -> prioritizer -> formatter -> END - linear, one SINGLE_AGENT dispatch.
gap_analyzer.dispatch: INTENT_TO_AGENTS['performance_gap'] -> gap_analyzer, criticality 'critical' (timeout 20s, no fallback); also fallback_agent for heterogeneous_optimizer's 'segment_analysis'; and first leg of MULTI_AGENT_PATTERNS[('performance_gap','resource_allocation')] as 'critical' (paired with resource_optimizer 'high').
gap_analyzer.distilled_line_verdict: correct: pipeline is now 5 business nodes, not 4 - instrument_analyzer (#357) sits between roi_calculator and prioritizer. Prioritization is a 3-bucket partition (quick_wins / steady_plays / strategic_bets) plus a suppressed value-destroying bucket (T6), not just quick-win/strategic-bet.
mismatches: agent.py module docstring still says 'Linear 4-node pipeline (gap_detector -> roi_calculator -> prioritizer -> formatter)', but graph.py wires 5 business nodes including instrument_analyzer - docstring is stale vs implementation.

tier-2 output contract (GapAnalyzerOutput) only defines quick_wins + strategic_bets, but the implementation output also emits steady_plays and suppressed_count (T6 3-bucket partition) - contract under-specifies the real output.
Docstring claims 'minimal LLM usage / Computational' (consistent with 20s SLA), but the instrument_analyzer IV F-test path is an implementation capability absent from the tier-2 contract prose.

heterogeneous_optimizer.purpose: Estimates treatment-effect heterogeneity (CATE) with EconML CausalForestDML, discovers high/low-responder segments, ranks effect-modifier importance, and recommends an optimal treatment-allocation policy across segments.
covers: Which HCP segments respond best (and worst) to increased engagement?
How does the treatment effect vary across segments - give me the CATE by segment?
Who are the high vs low responders and what features define them?
What's the optimal treatment-allocation policy across segments to maximize total lift?
Which effect modifiers drive the heterogeneity (feature importance)?
does_not_cover: The single overall ATE with full refutation/robustness and E-value sensitivity plus DAG construction - owned by causal_impact (heterogeneous_optimizer reports overall_ate as a byproduct but not the refutation/sensitivity suite).
ROI/opportunity sizing and payback across KPIs - owned by gap_analyzer (its fallback_agent).
Designing an experiment to validate the segment-specific strategies - owned by experiment_designer (its default suggested_next_agent).
Forecasting future outcomes - owned by prediction_synthesizer.
The org-wide constrained budget-allocation solve - owned by resource_optimizer (heterogeneous_optimizer emits per-segment PolicyRecommendation treatment rates, not the global optimizer solution).
heterogeneous_optimizer.internal_pipeline: audit_init -> estimate_cate (CausalForestDML CATE + heterogeneity_score + feature_importance) -> analyze_segments (high/low responders) -> [hierarchical_analysis (CausalML hierarchical uplift, optional)] -> [uplift_analysis (optional, non-fatal)] -> learn_policy (allocation policy) -> generate_profiles (viz + insights) -> END - one SINGLE_AGENT dispatch.
heterogeneous_optimizer.dispatch: INTENT_TO_AGENTS['segment_analysis'] -> heterogeneous_optimizer, criticality 'critical' (timeout 420000ms - raised for real CausalForestDML on the full frame, fallback_agent='gap_analyzer'); also second leg of MULTI_AGENT_PATTERNS[('causal_effect','segment_analysis')] as 'high'.
heterogeneous_optimizer.distilled_line_verdict: correct: confirm the CausalForestDML -> segment CATE -> high/low responders -> allocation policy core, but the distilled line omits two real stages - hierarchical uplift analysis (CausalML, toggleable) and the non-fatal uplift_analysis node - plus effect-modifier feature_importance and the generate_profiles (viz/insights) output.
mismatches: Contract latency says 'Up to 150s' but the router SLA is 420000ms (7 min); router comment documents a measured 269.7s serialized full-frame run, so the 150s contract figure is stale.

covers: Design an A/B test / RCT / quasi-experiment to validate that X causes Y (e.g. 'design an experiment to test whether higher HCP engagement raises TRx')
What sample size / duration do I need to detect a Z% effect at 80% power?
Choose a randomization strategy (unit, method, stratification, blocking, cluster adjustment with ICC)
Adversarially audit the validity of a proposed design and get mitigation recommendations (selection, confounding, contamination, attrition, external validity)
Generate a pre-registration document + DoWhy causal-model spec + Python analysis template for an experiment
Optionally digital-twin pre-screen an intervention before committing to the design (enable_twin_simulation, default OFF)
does_not_cover: Monitoring/health of an ALREADY-RUNNING experiment — SRM, enrollment, interim triggers, twin fidelity → experiment_monitor
Forecasting / ML point predictions → prediction_synthesizer
Estimating a causal effect (ATE) from existing observational data → causal_impact
Segment/CATE heterogeneity of an effect → heterogeneous_optimizer
experiment_designer.internal_pipeline: audit_init → context_loader → [optional twin_simulation pre-screen] → design_reasoning (real LLM) → power_analysis → validity_audit → (conditional redesign loop → power_analysis, capped at max_redesign_iterations) → template_generator → END (error_handler branch); one SINGLE_AGENT dispatch

drift_monitor.purpose: Detects temporal/distributional drift (data, model-prediction, concept, and causal-DAG structural) by comparing a current window against a baseline window with statistical tests, then aggregates a composite score and alerts.
covers: Has feature/input data drifted vs baseline? (PSI + KS on feature distributions)
Have model PREDICTIONS drifted / degraded over time? (KS on score dist, chi-square on class dist, PSI)
Has the feature->target relationship changed? (concept drift: feature-importance correlation + performance degradation across periods)
Has the causal DAG structure changed? (V4.4 structural drift: added/removed edges, edge-type changes, drift_score) - distinctive to this platform
Give me drift alerts with severity + recommended actions and an overall drift score over a time window
does_not_cover: Point-in-time 'is model X performing acceptably RIGHT NOW / what's its current accuracy/auc/latency' operational snapshot -> health_score (its model_health node)
Overall platform/component/pipeline/agent-availability health rollup -> health_score
Acting on drift (retraining, reallocating) -> not this agent
drift_monitor.internal_pipeline: audit_init -> data_drift -> model_drift -> concept_drift -> structural_drift (V4.4) -> alert_aggregator -> END (stateless; SupabaseDataConnector; no LLM)

SINGLE_AGENT.definition: Query maps to exactly ONE capability domain (is_multi_domain == False, i.e. domain_count <= 1), OR primary domain is EXPLANATION with confidence > 0.7. Routes to the one DOMAIN_TO_AGENT agent. Internal multi-step-ness of that agent is irrelevant - a single-domain query with dependent internal steps still routes here.
sources: router.py:300-315 (legacy single-agent dispatch on primary intent in INTENT_TO_AGENTS)

PARALLEL_DELEGATION.definition: Multi-domain (is_multi_domain == True) AND is_parallelizable == True (dependency_analysis has ZERO dependencies). Routes to multiple INDEPENDENT agents, one per detected domain, deduped. Legacy equivalent: hard-coded MULTI_AGENT_PATTERNS pairs, or Fix-1 primary+top-secondary parallel delegation.

TOOL_COMPOSER.definition: Multi-domain (Rule 3 already returned for single-domain) AND NOT parallelizable (has data dependencies between the cross-domain sub-questions). Docstring: 'Use Tool Composer for dependent multi-domain queries.' Routes to tool_composer. Legacy equivalent: primary_intent promoted to 'multi_faceted' only when a sequential/dependency marker joins >=2 DISTINCT strong intents and the pair is not a defined parallel pair.
sources: intent_classifier.py:429-450 (multi_faceted promotion: len(strong_components)>=2 + has_sequential_composition + not parallel pair)
multi_faceted.py:65-108 (sequential-marker SSOT; explicit 'single mapped intent wrongly routes single asks to tool_composer')

CLARIFICATION_NEEDED.definition: No domains detected, OR the top domain's confidence < MIN_CONFIDENCE (0.5). Query too ambiguous to route; returns empty target_agents, confidence 0.0. In router ACTIVE mode this pattern (or confidence < 0.5) causes the 4-stage pipeline to ABSTAIN and hand authority back to legacy intent routing rather than blocking.

composition_ruling.answer: Per the platform's own code, the criterion is 'no single agent's capability/domain covers the ask' (the query must span >=2 DISTINCT agent-capability domains, or >=2 distinct strong intents), AND those cross-domain sub-questions must be dependency-linked. 'Query decomposes into multiple dependent steps' is NOT sufficient on its own. If all steps live in ONE domain, the query routes SINGLE_AGENT no matter how many dependent internal steps it has - the domain agent (e.g. causal_impact) runs that multi-step pipeline itself under one dispatch. The dependency signal's ONLY job is to split a multi-DOMAIN query into PARALLEL_DELEGATION (no deps) vs TOOL_COMPOSER (deps). The LLM judge's rule ('needs multiple dependent steps -> TOOL_COMPOSER') is therefore WRONG by the platform's definition; the correct gate is cross-domain/cross-agent spanning first, dependency second.
evidence: pattern_selector.py:127-147 (Rule 3): `if not domain_mapping.is_multi_domain:` returns SINGLE_AGENT BEFORE dependency analysis is ever consulted for composition - single-domain can never reach TOOL_COMPOSER regardless of sub-questions/dependencies.
pattern_selector.py:194-212 (Rule 6): TOOL_COMPOSER is reachable only after Rule 3 (multi-domain established) AND Rule 5 fails (is_parallelizable False, i.e. dependencies exist).
schemas.py:129: is_multi_domain = len(domains_detected) > 1, where domains are distinct AGENT-CAPABILITY domains - the spanning test is over capabilities, not steps.

intent_classifier.py:429-450: promotion to 'multi_faceted' (->tool_composer) requires `len(strong_components) >= 2` DISTINCT strong intents PLUS has_sequential_composition PLUS not a defined parallel pair.

multi_faceted.py:65-75: explicit design comment - a bare 'then <verb>' from a SINGLE mapped intent 'wrongly routes single asks to the 180s tool_composer'; promotion happens ONLY when the marker joins '>=2 distinct strong intents'.
router.py:284-298: 'multi_faceted is a META-signal, not an agent domain'; dependent pipelines across >=2 intents go to tool_composer, a lone secondary meta-hint does not.
agent.py:245-247: tool_composer 'invoked by the Orchestrator when a query is classified as MULTI_FACETED - requiring capabilities from multiple agents combined in novel ways.'
